A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAS research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original RAS benchmark results in Table 1, component ablations, efficiency and sensitivity studies, and appendix training results.

after.justification: V2 retains original RAS evaluations and reports additional baseline results, triple-extractor comparisons in Table 3, and context-depth results and error cases in Appendix F.

M1.justification: V2 removes theme classification, query-to-document distribution shifting, and thematic corpus filtering, replacing v1's theme-scoped retrieval with direct retrieval over the corpus. It also specifies LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct instead of Flan-T5-Large as the default triple extractor. Shared-model multitask planning and answering already existed in v1.

E1.justification: DBPedia-298 classifier training and validation disappear with theme scoping. HotpotQA-SUBQ, WikiOFGraph, ARC-Easy/ASQA training, both Wikipedia knowledge sources, and all seven evaluation benchmarks remain. The added analyses do not introduce a new task or domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LLaMA-3-8B baselines with and without retrieval and Search-R1-7B. Comparator coverage also expands within existing benchmarks: SuRe-7B gains comparisons on TriviaQA, PopQA, PubHealth, ARC and ELI5; SuRe-GPT gains ELI5; RPG-7B gains TriviaQA and ARC. The existing comparator suite is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a retrieval-depth control using 5, 10 and 15 documents and expands extractor comparisons to three models. V1's theme-filtering settings and 100-sample CPU timing protocol disappear. Retained benchmark sample sizes, metrics, generation limits, iteration limits, and zero-/few-shot evaluation designs remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the theme-scoping ablation and efficiency study. It expands v1 Appendix E.2's brief extractor-quality observation into a three-extractor study, and adds context-depth analysis and two contrasting graph-construction cases in Appendix F. Training-volume, graph-information and most component ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average the graph-information experiment over five random triple shuffles and retain the same reporting practice (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 3). V2 introduces no new seed disclosure, repeated-run uncertainty reporting, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline, extractor and context-depth results and removes theme-related results. Several main-table RAS values change, including RAS-7B ARC accuracy from 67.7 to 68.5 and TriviaQA accuracy from 72.6 to 72.7. These are revised results under a changed pipeline, not established same-setting gains. Table 2 also fills the previously blank ASQA No Planning entries.

T1.justification: The formal retrieval specification changes: v1's query/document theme-distribution mappings and theme-selected subcorpus formulation in Equations 3–6 are replaced by direct corpus retrieval in v2 Equation 3. Graph construction definitions, the sample-labeling algorithm and metric formulas are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 drops theme-scoped retrieval and its efficiency advantage from the main contributions, refocusing the paper on dynamic graph construction and structure-aware planning and answering. Its abstract also qualifies the retained 6.4% and 7.0% figures as gains 'up to' those amounts, replacing v1's blanket across-metrics wording.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of diminishing returns from larger retrieved contexts and failures caused by missing or misleading triples, and expands interpretations of partial-graph robustness. It removes the obsolete theme-classifier temporal limitation and explicitly distinguishes RAS from KGQA-focused methods. Most existing interpretations and remaining limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 removes the extensive classifier/shifter architectures, training settings and hyperparameter documentation. It documents LLaMA-3.2 triple-extractor training and vLLM deployment, adds a code-and-data availability statement, and supplies an asset/source/license inventory in Table 8. Core GraphLLM hardware, training settings and prompts remain; both extractor checkpoint links already appeared in v1.

R1.justification: V2 introduces an interpretability-based rationale using Lindsey et al., adds a first-application claim for Graph LLMs in general language generation, and explicitly positions RAS relative to KGQA methods such as Think-on-Graph and Reasoning on Graphs. It adds Search-R1, DeepRetrieval and other references while removing theme-component references, substantially revising the novelty framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related work are extensively rewritten. The method becomes a three-stage presentation with key definitions and a dedicated multitask-learning subsection. Terminology is revised throughout, impact discussion moves into an expanded appendix, supplementary analyses are inserted, and the standalone notation appendix is removed.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two-column to single-column layout and redraws the overview, extension and running-example diagrams. It restructures Table 1, redisplays the short-form/closed-set role-swapping results as Figure 2, removes efficiency and classifier/shifter plots, and adds extractor, context-depth and asset tables. Retained sensitivity plots are relocated.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons, task-specific extractor evidence and larger-context controls make the retained structuring claim better supported and easier to assess than in v1. The revised exposition also clarifies the shared-model design. These gains accompany a narrower contribution after theme scoping is removed. Uncertainty reporting remains limited, and v2 Tables 1 and 6 give inconsistent RAS-Sonnet PubHealth/ARC values, limiting the overall improvement.
